description: Browse and retrieve U.S. congressional amendments from Congress.gov — House (hamdt), Senate (samdt), and Senate unprinted (suamdt, 97th and 98th Congresses only). An amendment is addressed by congress + amendmentType + amendmentNumber, the identifiers other tools return: congressgov_bill_lookup 'amendments' rows (type and number), House votes from congressgov_roll_votes (amendmentType and amendmentNumber), and amendment rows from congressgov_member_lookup 'sponsored'/'cosponsored' (amendmentNumber, with the type in the row's url); either letter case is accepted. Use 'list' to browse one congress, optionally one amendmentType (newest update first; fromDateTime/toDateTime filter on update date), 'get' for the record (sponsor, purpose, description, the bill or amendment it amends, latest action), or drill in with 'actions', 'cosponsors', 'amendments' (amendments to this amendment), or 'text'. 'text' lists the published text versions — the Congressional Record pages that print the amendment, often alongside the surrounding floor proceedings — and 'content' reads one version's HTML as plain text, a bounded character window at a time. On that page a Senate amendment is printed under 'SA {number}' or 'Amendment No. {number}'; a House amendment is not printed under its HAMDT number — find it at the Record page its 'actions' rows cite ('text: CR H3582-3583' is the '[[Page H3582]]' marker) or under 'Amendment No. N Offered by', where N is the number the description from 'get' gives it ('An amendment numbered 64 printed in House Report 118-142'). An 'actions' row that records a roll call vote carries rollVote — the chamber, congress, session, and voteNumber congressgov_roll_votes takes to return that vote and each member's position.

anyOf.description: Digit-string form, as list rows carry it.

amendmentNumber.description: Amendment number. Required for every operation but 'list', which refuses it. Accepts the digit-string form rows carry (e.g. "255") as well as a number.

amendmentType.description: Amendment type: 'hamdt' (House), 'samdt' (Senate), or 'suamdt' (Senate unprinted, 97th and 98th Congresses only). Optional on 'list'; required for every other operation.

characterLimit.description: Maximum characters to return for 'content' (1-100000). Legislative documents run past a million characters, so a full bill takes several windows.

characterOffset.description: First character to return for 'content', 0-based. Offsets are exact and are never snapped to a section or paragraph break, so feeding the response's nextOffset back walks the whole document with every character returned exactly once.

fromDateTime.description: Start of the update-date window for 'list' (ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z): when Congress.gov last touched the record, not when the amendment was offered. Other operations ignore it and say so in the notice.

order.description: Sort order for 'list' (sorts by update date). 'recent' (default) is newest first; 'oldest' is ascending. Ignored by other operations.

textVersionIndex.description: Which text version 'content' reads, 0-based against the order 'text' returns. Ignored by other operations.

toDateTime.description: End of the update-date window for 'list' (ISO 8601). Same field semantics as fromDateTime.

name: congressgov_amendment_lookup

data.description: Result rows for `list` and the sub-resource operations.

items.description: Upstream JSON record: an amendment (`list`, `amendments`) or a sub-resource row. An `actions` row carries `rollVote` when it records one roll call vote congressgov_roll_votes serves.

rollVote.description: Arguments for congressgov_roll_votes that retrieve the roll call vote this action records — its one recordedVotes entry. Absent when the action records no vote or several, and for a vote that tool has no data for: Congress.gov publishes House roll call votes from the 115th Congress (2017) onward, and the Senate publishes roll call votes from the 101st Congress (1989) onward.

chamber.description: Chamber the vote was cast in. Pass it: congressgov_roll_votes defaults to 'house', and roll call numbers are specific to one chamber.

congress.description: Congress the vote was cast in.

session.description: Session the vote was cast in (1 or 2); roll call numbers restart each session.

effectiveQuery.description: The browse scope and applied filters.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `not_found`: A requested bill, member, committee, report, vote, or nomination does not exist in Congress.gov. `rate_limited`: A process-local attempt budget or the shared upstream credential/IP quota was reached; upstream hourly limits vary and DEMO_KEY also has a daily quota. On a Senate vote the LIS feed could not answer, Voteview answering HTTP 429 is reported the same way. `invalid_request`: Congress.gov rejected the request as malformed — a bad date range or an identifier with an unexpected shape. `api_key_rejected`: The api.data.gov gateway rejected the server's configured CONGRESS_API_KEY (missing, invalid, disabled, unauthorized, or unverified); the gateway code is in data.upstreamCode. No change to the call's arguments can fix it. `upstream_error`: Congress.gov returned an unexpected error (5xx or another non-2xx status) or could not be reached, or a Senate vote could be read from neither the Senate LIS feed nor its Voteview fallback (before the 101st Congress there is no fallback, and there a senate.gov HTTP 403 refusal carries retryable: false). `upstream_timeout`: A Congress.gov request or a congress.gov document fetch timed out or returned an HTTP timeout response, or the call's upstream requests could not finish inside its 50-second budget. `document_unavailable`: The 'content' selection resolves to no retrievable document — the text version or article index is past the end of the list, the record publishes no formats at all, or Congress.gov does not hold the file its own metadata names. `format_unavailable`: The document exists but publishes nothing in a format this server reads — some text versions and committee reports ship PDF only, no Congressional Record article publishes XML, and the oldest CRS reports publish a PDF but no HTML. `document_fetch_failed`: www.congress.gov did not return a readable document — a non-2xx status, a network failure, an empty body, or a content type that is not text or XML. `document_too_large`: The document is larger than the byte ceiling this server retrieves, so no character window can be served from it. `offset_past_end`: characterOffset is at or beyond the last character of every text the call would window — the document on 'content', or every returned row's summary text on 'summaries' — so the window would be empty. `incompatible_identity`: A list operation carries an entity identifier that only a detail operation uses. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

notice.description: Guidance when results are empty, a page is past the end, or a caveat applies.

pagination.description: Pagination metadata: total count and next offset.

count.description: Total result count across all pages.

nextOffset.description: Offset to pass for the next page, or null when there are no more pages.

title: Congress.gov Amendment Lookup
